title: Arrays
summary: Scan, prefix and suffix, sliding window, two pointers, Kadane

guide.title: The most common input in coding rounds
points: Around half of placement coding questions give you an array. Strings, matrices and DP tables are arrays too.
Elements sit next to each other in memory, so reading a[i] is instant (O(1)) and scanning is fast.
A few patterns (prefix sums, sliding window, two pointers, Kadane) turn slow O(n²) answers into O(n).

guide.title: Where arrays work for you
points: Stock apps: daily prices are an array; "best time to buy and sell" and "biggest gain over a period" are array scans (Kadane).
Monitoring dashboards: the moving average of CPU use or sensor readings over the last k minutes is a sliding window.
Analytics: total sales between two dates in O(1) after one prefix-sum pass.
Search results from two sorted lists are merged with two pointers; images are arrays of pixels.

guide.title: Index, length, one pass
points: Positions run from 0 to length − 1. Reading past the end is the most common crash.
Most questions need one pass: keep the best value, a count or a running sum as you go.
Ask: do I need a new array, or can I change this one in place?

guide.title: Create, loop, find the largest
points: Each language has a "for each" loop for reading and an index loop when you need the position.

code.python:
nums = [3, 9, 2]
best = nums[0]
for x in nums:
    best = max(best, x)
print(len(nums), best)   # 3 9

guide.title: Prefix sums: any range total in O(1)
points: prefix[i] = sum of the first i elements. Then the sum of a[l..r] is prefix[r + 1] − prefix[l].
One O(n) pass, then every query is instant: the trick behind "subarray sum equals k" and range-total questions.

code.python:
prefix = [0]
for x in a:
    prefix.append(prefix[-1] + x)
range_sum = lambda l, r: prefix[r + 1] - prefix[l]

guide.title: Sliding window and two pointers
points: Sliding window: for "best block of k in a row", add the element entering the window and remove the one leaving it. O(n) instead of O(n·k).
Two pointers: on a sorted array, start at both ends; if the pair sum is too small move left, too big move right.
Kadane: for the largest subarray sum, at each element either extend the current run or start again: cur = max(x, cur + x).

guide.title: What breaks array code
points: Reading a[i + 1] or a[i − 1] at the edges: check the first and last index.
An empty array: a[0] does not exist. Decide what the answer is when there is nothing.
Assuming the array is sorted, or sorting it when the original order matters.
Two nested loops on 10⁵ elements is 10¹⁰ steps: a time-out. Look for a one-pass pattern.

guide.title: For advanced learners and interviews
points: Size → target: n ≤ 10³ allows O(n²); n ≤ 10⁵ needs O(n log n) or O(n).
In-place tricks: swap with a write pointer (move zeroes), reverse parts of the array (rotate by k), Dutch national flag (three-way partition).
Interview flow: say the brute force and its cost first, then improve it with one of these patterns. It shows how you think.
Next step: Strings, which are arrays of characters with a few extra rules.

problems.title: Largest element
problems.statement: Return the largest value in a non-empty array.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Keep the best seen so far.

problems.title: Second largest
problems.statement: Return the second largest distinct value, or -1 if there is none.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Track the largest and the second largest in one pass.

problems.title: Move zeroes to the end
problems.statement: Move all zeroes to the end while keeping the order of the other elements. Return the array.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Use a write pointer for the non-zero values.

problems.title: Pair with a given sum
problems.statement: nums is sorted in increasing order. Return the 1-based positions of two different elements that add to target, or [-1] if none. If several pairs exist, return the one with the smallest first position.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)

problems.title: Maximum sum of k in a row
problems.statement: Return the largest sum of k consecutive elements (1 <= k <= length).
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Slide a window: add the new element, remove the oldest.

problems.title: Product except self
problems.statement: Return an array where position i holds the product of all elements except nums[i]. Do not use division.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Multiply a prefix pass and a suffix pass.

problems.title: Maximum subarray sum
problems.statement: Return the largest sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Kadane: extend the current run or start a new one.

problems.title: Trapping rain water
problems.statement: Bars of width 1 have the given heights. Return how many units of water are held between them after rain.
inputFormat: height: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Water at i = min(highest left, highest right) - height. Two pointers do it in one pass.
